caseno: Appeal from original Decree No. 69 of 1982.
lawyer:
K. M. Raisuddin Khan ------ For the Appellant.
M.I. Farruqi with M.A. Wahab ------ For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Md. Fazlur Rahman & others ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Mrs. Bani Rahman, wife of Sk. Lutfur Rahman & Ors ------ Respondent.
full_judgment: 4. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the facts and circumstances adduced in the case held that the suit has been brought for a declaration that the ex-parte Judgment and decree dated 27.7.77 passed in Title Suit No. 3 of 1977 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is void, illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs and is liable to be set aside. He further found that possession have been delivered through Court to the defendant No. 1 and the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession therein by any independent witness and as such the present suit for declaration without any prayer for recovery of khas possession is not maintainable. Ho also found that the question of the plaintiffs in the suit property is seriously involved and without establishment of declaration of their title in the suit property, the plaintiffs cannot have any locus standi to challenge that decree. He also found that in the present suit, there was no prayer for establishment or declaration of the plaintiffs' title in the suit property. He also opined that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and that it is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He therefore dismissed the suit. As against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred this appeal before this Court and contended that the plaintiffs were not a party and the decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree as prayed for. The present suit is a suit for declaration that the said ex-parte decree is void. He was within his competency in the said suit to get a declaration to that effect in View of the fact that he was not a party in the original suit. In order to obtain a decree to the effect that the decree was void the person seeking such a relief has to prove his title to the suit property. Unless be can prove his title to the suit property he cannot have the luxury of having a decree declared to be void, in the present case it is found that the defendants are in possession in the suit property by virtue of previous title suit. So in the facts and circumstances of the case the plaintiffs are not entitled to any such declaration as prayed for. They can file a properly constituted suit for declaration of their title as also for declaration that the decree with regard to the property was void. It does not require any declaration by the Court that a decree is not binding on a person who is not a party to the suit. If he wants to have such a declaration he is to prove his title to the suit property, otherwise he is not entitled to get such a declaration. In the present case the plaintiffs have not established their title. As such the learned Judge was right in holding that the suit was barred under the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In that view of the matter we find that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. In that view of the matter this appeal is dismissed with costs.
